_comment: Golden-corpus regression fixtures for build_dispatch_plan()'s deterministic
selector. Each case is run through build_dispatch_plan() in standalone
mode (Agentic SDLC lifecycle contract forced unavailable, see
test_selection_golden_corpus.py) so the corpus is reproducible without
AGENTIC_SDLC_BIN or network access. 'expected' compares exactly against
the four build_dispatch_plan() output fields named in the requirements
baseline (primary, reviewers, support, matched_routes); 'team_ids' is an
optional fifth field asserted only for cases whose purpose is to pin a
team_recipes trigger. Task strings reused verbatim from
test_selector.py/test_agents_dispatcher.py are noted in 'description' so
this corpus does not silently drift from those regression tests.
A route/keyword edit that changes any of these fields must update this
file in the same reviewable diff (see CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and B-FR-6).
Coverage: this corpus covers every route category defined in
routing.yaml's routes[] array, matching B-FR-5's 'initial corpus covers
every existing route category' requirement. The route id list is not
enumerated here because it drifts every time a route is added, removed,
or renamed -- routing.yaml's routes[] array is the live list;
test_corpus_covers_every_required_route_category in
test_selection_golden_corpus.py is the enforcement, reading routing.yaml
directly rather than any count or enumeration recorded in this comment.
Most single-route fixtures were
authored fresh (not reused from test_selector.py) specifically to
isolate one route per case; where routing.yaml's own paths/keywords
genuinely overlap between two or more routes (e.g. testing and
black-box-testing both list **/*.feature; backend and
database-reliability both list 'postgresql' as a keyword), the fixture
description says so explicitly rather than treating the extra matched
route as an authoring mistake. The corpus also separately pins the
'production' and 'destructive' risk_rules with distinct fixtures
(PRODUCTION-RISK-1, DESTRUCTIVE-RISK-1) since they have separate
keyword_groups, human_gate, and reviewers in routing.yaml and one does
not stand in for the other. A future routing.yaml edit that adds,
removes, or renames a route category must update this comment and the
corresponding fixture(s) in the same diff, and
test_corpus_covers_every_required_route_category in
test_selection_golden_corpus.py enforces that every route id currently
in routing.yaml is represented in this file's matched_routes.

cases.description: #189 review finding 2: root pyproject.toml is deliberately NOT a packaging-route path. It is a generic file present in arbitrary downstream Python projects, and routing.yaml ships as the BASE ruleset to every consuming project (routing_overlay.py only lets a consumer widen a base route, never narrow it) -- claiming it under a route named 'packaging' whose keywords are about this repo's own Cline ports and plugin manifests would be wrong for every consumer. A pyproject.toml-only change with no packaging keyword (and no other route's keyword -- the task text deliberately avoids change_intake baseline words like 'update'/'change' and supply-chain's 'dependency' so the result is genuinely needs-triage, not just support-only) is therefore needs-triage, not the packaging route. kernel/pyproject.toml, engine/pyproject.toml, root pyproject.toml, and cadre_cli/__init__.py all remain unrouted, a documented out-of-scope adjacent gap for a follow-up issue.
cases.task: Look at pyproject.toml

cases.description: #189 re-review finding 1 (code-reviewer, MEDIUM; revision 2) pin: packaging/plugin-README.md routes through agent-suite-governance ONLY. The packaging route no longer carries packaging/** at all -- copying agent-suite-governance's pre-existing imprecise glob onto a second route was not a license to double that imprecision's blast radius, and routing.yaml ships as a base ruleset a consumer can only widen, never narrow. The packaging route is now scoped to plugin/tools/** only. Staffing for this file is unaffected (agent-suite-governance's primary/reviewers are byte-identical to the packaging route's), only matched_routes visibility changes. The extra documentation route match (**/*.md) is incidental and unrelated to this decision.
